title: Orders without a seal
body:
Around 1510. Tun Mutahir has been put to death on Sultan Mahmud's order. Paduka Tuan is bendahara now, and Mahmud yields the throne to his son Ahmad.

A rice seller brings yesterday's order for the royal store. No one will countersign it, and the seller won't unload on credit. There is room at the public scales if you send the boat there instead.

choices.label: Direct the rice to the public scales
choices.outcome_text: The seller is paid in the market. The royal storekeeper goes home with an empty tally.

choices.label: Ask the seller to wait for a fresh royal order
choices.outcome_text: The storekeeper keeps the first claim on the load, but no rice from this boat reaches the market tonight.

notes: fact: Mahmud ordered Tun Mutahir's execution; Paduka Tuan replaced him and Mahmud yielded the throne to Ahmad. Accounts give different motives for the execution (docs/research/1511-events.md §§1, 4.3).
inference: The purge weakened the court's administrative and commercial relationships before the invasion (docs/research/1511-events.md §1, Phase II).
gameplay: The unsigned purchase order, credit refusal and rice disposition are invented.
